admin.title: Administration
admin.resetWarn: A new random password will be generated and shown once. Their old password stops working, they are signed out everywhere, and the reset appears in their own activity log.
admin.newPasswordBody: Share this password securely. It won't be shown again.
admin.inviteRegistration: Allow registration with an invite link
admin.mcpHint: Endpoint /mcp. Needs a user's access token and only reaches what that token allows. Off answers 404.
admin.sessionIdleHint: Default 30. Cannot exceed the absolute lifetime.
admin.sessionMaxHint: Default 90. Everyone signs in again after this long, however active.
admin.retentionHint: Older entries are deleted automatically once a day.
admin.limitsHint: Set a value to 0 to restore the built-in default.
admin.kindsHint: Users can only add channels for the services checked here.
admin.egressGuard: Block notifications to private network addresses
admin.egressHint: Recommended. Turn off only if you need to reach services on your own network (for example a self-hosted ntfy).
admin.egressLocked: Always on in hosted mode and can't be changed.
updates.title: Updates
updates.current: You are up to date. Latest release: {v}
updates.unconfirmed: You're running {running}. Couldn't confirm the latest release yet.
updates.checkOffHint: Turn on the background check to look for updates.
updates.enable: Check for updates in the background
updates.privacy: The check fetches the public release information from GitHub with a generic user agent. It sends no information about this server.
admin.requirePow: Require a quick proof-of-work check when signing up
limit.email_codes_account_hour: Sign-in codes emailed per account per hour
limit.emails_ip_hour: Emails per IP address per hour
limit.invites_per_household_day: Invite links created per household per 24 hours (revoked ones count too)
limit.signups_per_ip_hour: Sign-ups per IP address per hour
limit.ai_requests_per_user_day: AI chore suggestions per user per day
admin.inactiveHint: Warn people who have not signed in for a long time, then delete their account. Off by default.
admin.inactiveDeleteHint: At least 30 days after the warning. A final warning goes out 30 days before deletion. Instance admins are never deleted.
proxy.title: Reverse proxy not trusted
proxy.body: Gunkly received requests from {peers} that carry forwarding headers, but that address is not in the trusted proxy list. Until it is, client addresses in the activity log and sessions show the proxy's address, and per-address limits treat every visitor as one, so everyone shares a single sign-in rate limit.
proxy.fix: If that address is your reverse proxy, add this to the Gunkly environment and restart:
proxy.docs: Read how to set up a reverse proxy
proxy.shared: Only add addresses you control. Anything listed there is believed when it says who the visitor is.
admin.oauthEnabled: Let apps such as ChatGPT sign in with Gunkly (OAuth)
admin.oauthHint: Lets apps that cannot take an access key (ChatGPT, Claude connectors) sign in to /mcp. Off by default; answers 404 while off. Needs public HTTPS at GUNKLY_BASE_URL.
admin.webhooksEnabled: Let household owners add outgoing webhooks
admin.webhooksHint: Gunkly then sends signed JSON to the web addresses owners add, for example to a home automation system. Off by default: while off, nothing is sent and the settings are hidden.
admin.group.limitsHint: Usage limits per user and household
admin.ssoCreateAccounts: Create accounts for new single sign-on users
admin.ssoCreateAccountsHint: When someone signs in with single sign-on for the first time and no account is linked to them, Gunkly creates one (username from their provider profile, no password). Off by default: they then see a message to link an existing account. Accounts are never matched by email.
admin.ssoName: Name on the single sign-on button
admin.ssoNameHint: Shown as "Sign in with …" (for example Authelia or Keycloak). Empty: "Sign in with SSO".
admin.ssoNameHintDefault: Shown as "Sign in with …". Empty: the name from GUNKLY_OIDC_NAME ({name}).
admin.ssoHosted: Single sign-on is not available on this hosted service.
admin.ssoStep1: At your provider, create an OpenID Connect application (confidential client, authorization code flow) with this redirect URI:
config.locked: Set by {env} in the server's environment
aiAdmin.title: AI chore suggestions
aiAdmin.intro: Optional. When it's on, people can describe chores in their own words ("vacuum every Saturday, Sam and Alex take turns on the dishes") and get suggestions to check before anything is added. It works with any service that speaks the OpenAI API:
aiAdmin.paid: A paid service, such as OpenAI or Mistral: use its API address and a key from your account there. Each suggestion costs a little.
aiAdmin.local: A model on your own network, such as Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp: use its address (for Ollama http://<host>:11434/v1). Usually no key, and nothing leaves your network.
aiAdmin.privacy: For each request Gunkly sends the typed text, the household's area names, members' names and today's date. Nothing else.
aiAdmin.urlHint: The base address that ends in /v1. Addresses on your own network are allowed here.
aiAdmin.modelHint: The model's name as the service knows it, for example gpt-4o-mini or llama3.1.
aiAdmin.keyHint: Stored encrypted and never shown again. Leave empty for a local model that needs none.
aiAdmin.testOk: It works: the model answered in {ms} ms.
aiAdmin.limitHint: How often each person can ask per day is set under Limits (50 by default).
aiAdmin.fail.unreachable: Can't reach that address. Check the address and that the service is running and reachable from this server.
aiAdmin.fail.auth: The service refused the key. Check the API key.
aiAdmin.fail.notFound: Nothing found there. Check that the address ends in /v1 and that the model name is right.
aiAdmin.fail.rateLimited: The service is limiting requests (or the account has no credit left).
aiAdmin.fail.timeout: No answer in time. A local model may still be loading; try again in a minute.
aiAdmin.fail.badResponse: The service answered, but not like an OpenAI-compatible API.
svcAdmin.emailIntro: Optional. With email set up, people can add an address to reset a forgotten password, get sign-in codes and receive reminders by email. Gunkly sends through an SMTP server you already have: your mail provider's, or a service such as Mailgun or Postmark.
svcAdmin.emailEnableHint: Needs at least the server and the From address.
svcAdmin.smtpFromHint: For example Gunkly <gunkly@example.com>. Your mail server must be allowed to send as this address.
svcAdmin.secretHint: Stored encrypted and never shown again.
svcAdmin.emailTestOk: Sent to {to}. Check the inbox (and the spam folder).
svcAdmin.emailTestFail: Sending failed. Check the server, port, encryption and login, and that this server may connect to it (Connections, outbound protection blocks addresses on your own network).
svcAdmin.incomplete: Not running: some required details are missing.
svcAdmin.needsHttps: Not running: single sign-on needs this server's address (GUNKLY_BASE_URL) to start with https://.
svcAdmin.ssoIntro: Let people sign in with your own OpenID Connect provider, such as Authelia, authentik, Keycloak or Pocket ID. Accounts are linked by the provider's user ID, never by email address.
svcAdmin.issuerHint: The provider's address exactly as in its discovery document (https).
svcAdmin.ssoTestOk: The provider answers (sign-in page at {origin}). Try a real sign-in to check the client ID and secret.
svcAdmin.ssoTestFail: The provider can't be reached or doesn't answer as an OpenID Connect provider. Check the address.
svcAdmin.metricsIntro: With a token set, /metrics serves Prometheus metrics to a scraper that sends it as a bearer token. Without one, /metrics does not exist.
svcAdmin.metricsTokenHint: At least 16 characters, for example from: openssl rand -hex 24. Stored encrypted and never shown again.
svcAdmin.powMaxHint: How much work a browser does before an open sign-up is accepted (1000 to 1000000; default 250000). Higher slows down bots and people alike.
updates.updating: Update requested. Gunkly restarts when the new version is ready; this page reloads by itself.
updates.updateTimeout: No new version after 5 minutes. Check your updater's logs.
updates.hookRejected: The updater refused the request (HTTP {status}). Check the address and token under Update button.
updates.hookUnreachable: Couldn't reach the updater. Check the address under Update button and that it's running.
svcAdmin.hookIntro: Gunkly can't update itself. If you run an updater that can be started with a web request, enter it here and an "Update now" button appears above when a new version is out. Gunkly sends it one POST request; the updater pulls the new image and restarts Gunkly.
svcAdmin.hookWhy: Why not built in: updating itself would need access to Docker, which is the same as full control of the server. Anyone who broke into Gunkly would get that too. This way Gunkly can only ask, and your updater decides. Works with Watchtower, Portainer, Dockhand or your own script.
svcAdmin.hookKindHint: Only Dockhand changes what is sent (it is asked to pull the newest image first); the others get the same request.
svcAdmin.hookUrlHint: Watchtower: http://watchtower:8080/v1/update. Portainer: the webhook URL of Gunkly's stack or container (turn on its webhook and "Re-pull image"). Dockhand: https://<dockhand>/api/stacks/<stack name>/deploy?env=<environment ID>. Addresses on your own network are allowed.
svcAdmin.hookTokenHint: Sent as "Authorization: Bearer …". Watchtower: its HTTP API token. Dockhand: an API token (dh_…) from your Dockhand profile. Portainer: leave empty, the webhook URL is the secret. Stored encrypted and never shown again.
guide.addressIntro: Gunkly puts this address in emails, reminders and calendar links. It is set in the server's environment (GUNKLY_BASE_URL), not here, because links, sign-in cookies and passkeys depend on it.
guide.addressOk: All good: the configured address matches and uses https.
guide.addressMissing: No address is configured. Set GUNKLY_BASE_URL to the address people use (for example https://chores.example.com) in your docker-compose file and restart Gunkly; until then links in emails and reminders won't work.
guide.addressMismatch: The configured address ({base}) is not the one you opened ({here}). If people use {here}, set GUNKLY_BASE_URL to it and restart Gunkly.
guide.addressHttp: The address doesn't use https. Gunkly works, but passkeys, single sign-on and AI assistant connectors need https. A reverse proxy such as Caddy can add it.
guide.addressWhy: Everything in the next steps can be set right here, without touching Docker. You can skip any step and change it later under Administration.
guide.emailIntro: Without email, people sign in with a user name and you reset forgotten passwords yourself. With email, they can reset passwords, use email codes and get reminders by email.
guide.signinIntro: Everyone can sign in with a password, and add a passkey or an authenticator app. If you run your own identity provider, you can let people use it here.
guide.signinMore: Open sign-up, invite rules and session lengths are under
guide.notifyIntro: Nothing to set up here: each person chooses how they get reminders, in their own Settings, Notifications.
guide.notifyPush: Browser and phone notifications work out of the box (on iPhone, after adding Gunkly to the home screen).
guide.notifyApps: People can also connect messaging apps such as Telegram, Discord, Slack, ntfy or Pushover, with step-by-step help.
guide.notifyHousehold: A household can share one channel too, for example the family group chat.
guide.notifyAdmin: Which messaging services are allowed, and the outbound protection, are under
guide.aiIntro: Let people describe chores in their own words and get suggestions to check. Skip this if you don't want it; it stays off.
guide.updatesIntro: Gunkly can tell you when a new version is out, and optionally ask an updater you run to install it.
guide.doneIntro: Everything here can be changed later under Administration. Next, create your household and invite the people you live with.
guide.doneUsers: Add accounts for others (or invite them from the household)
guide.againLead: Email, sign-in, AI and updates step by step:
admin.securityAlertsHint: Emails the admins (with a confirmed address) about suspicious activity, such as a household creating invite links up to the daily limit. At most one email per household per day; the events are always listed on the Administration page.
secEvents.title: Recent security events
secEvents.intro: Worth a look: these happened in the last 7 days.
secEvents.invite_limit_reached: {username} hit the daily invite limit in household {household}
secEvents.email_failing: Email delivery started failing: confirmation emails and sign-in codes are not arriving
emailFailing.title: Email delivery is failing
emailFailing.body: Gunkly has not been able to send email since {since}. Confirmation links and sign-in codes cannot be delivered, so people may be unable to sign up or sign in with an email code.
emailFailing.reason.connect: Latest error: the mail server could not be reached.
emailFailing.reason.tls: Latest error: a secure (TLS) connection to the mail server could not be set up.
emailFailing.reason.auth: Latest error: the mail server refused the username or password.
emailFailing.reason.timeout: Latest error: the mail server took too long to answer.
emailFailing.reason.refused: Latest error: the mail server refused to accept the message.
emailFailing.reason.other: Latest error: the message could not be sent.
emailFailing.fix: Check the SMTP settings under Administration, Email, and the status of your mail provider. This warning goes away as soon as an email is sent.
secEvents.hint: Each of these can be a sign of abuse or an attack. Check the account under Users; the audit log has the details. Emails about them can be turned off under Sign-up & sign-in, Security alerts.
